step1_figure.circuit_type: CMOS Op-Amp with Output Buffer (Cascode Diff-Amp with Class-AB Push-Pull Output Stage and Indirect Compensation)
step1_figure.description: Figure 24.29 shows a two-stage op-amp combining a high-gain cascode differential first stage with a push-pull class-AB output buffer (MON/MOP) and indirect feedback frequency compensation via capacitor Cc connected to the source of cascode device M2T.

open_loop_dc_gain.description: Low-frequency open-loop differential voltage gain without external resistive load

equation.explanation: Overall DC open-loop gain is the product of the first-stage cascode diff-amp gain A1 (~500 V/V) and the second-stage push-pull gain A2 (~31.6 V/V).
equation.assumptions: Unloaded output, transistors in saturation, nominal bias currents from Fig. 20.47 bias network.

sky130_expected.calculation: In SKY130 (1.8V): With gm ~ 150 uS and cascode output resistance ~ 3.3 MOhm, stage 1 gain A1 ~ 500 V/V (54 dB). Stage 2 push-pull with 10x current conducts ~100 uA, gm ~ 1 mS, ro ~ 33 kOhm, giving A2 ~ 30-33 V/V (30 dB). Total unloaded gain A_OLDC = 500 * 31.6 = 15,800 V/V ~ 84 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Lower channel length modulation resistance in short-channel SKY130 devices may slightly reduce cascode gain compared to long-channel approximations.

second_stage_gain.description: Voltage gain of the push-pull output buffer stage under no load

equation.explanation: The output buffer stage transconductance is sum of NMOS and PMOS transconductances, driving parallel output resistance of MOP and MON.
equation.assumptions: Quiescent current = 100 uA, no external resistive load connected to Vout.

sky130_expected.calculation: At Iq = 100 uA, gmn_eff ~ 0.8 mS, gmp_eff ~ 0.4 mS, rout_eff ~ (ron || rop)/10 ~ 25 kOhm. A2 = -(0.8m + 0.4m)*25k ~ -30 V/V = 29.5 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Consistent with Baker's derived Eq. (24.36) giving 31.6 V/V (30 dB).

unity_gain_frequency.description: Unity-gain frequency (gain-bandwidth product fun) of the open-loop op-amp

equation.explanation: Determined by the transconductance of the input differential pair and the indirect compensation capacitance Cc = 240 fF.

sky130_expected.calculation: With input pair tail current Iss = 30 uA (15 uA per branch), gm1 = sqrt(2 * un * Cox * (W/L) * Id) ~ 150 uA/V. fun = 150e-6 / (2 * pi * 240e-15) ~ 99.5 MHz, matching Fig. 24.30 (~100 MHz).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Parasitic capacitances at node 1 and the indirect feedback node slightly shift the zero and pole.

phase_margin.description: Phase margin of the open-loop op-amp at unity gain frequency

equation.explanation: Phase margin ensures stable closed-loop operation without excessive ringing.

sky130_expected.calculation: As stated on page 794: 'The open-loop response of the op-amp in Fig. 24.29 (without a load) is seen in Fig. 24.30. The phase-margin is roughly 70 degrees.'
sky130_expected.reasoning: Indirect compensation eliminates the RHP zero present in standard Miller compensation, maintaining PM ~ 70 deg.

closed_loop_settling_time.description: Settling time (10% to 90% or 1% of final value) for an inverting closed-loop configuration driving 1k ohm and 10 pF

equation.explanation: Under closed-loop gain ACL = -1 with R1=10k, R2=10k, RL=1k, CL=10pF, response settles rapidly within a few nanoseconds.
equation.assumptions: Step input 100 mV to 900 mV, common-mode voltage = 500 mV.

sky130_expected.calculation: From Fig. 24.31, for an input step transitioning at 520 ns and 560 ns, output completes transition from 900 mV to 100 mV (and back) within ~5-15 ns.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Low output resistance of push-pull buffer allows driving 1k || 10pF with minimal slew-rate limitation.

slew_rate.description: Maximum rate of output voltage change during large-signal step transient

equation.explanation: Differential input stage tail current charging/discharging compensation capacitor Cc.

sky130_expected.calculation: With Iss ~ 30 uA and Cc = 240 fF, SR ~ 30 uA / 240 fF = 125 V/us (125 mV/ns). For the output stage driving CL=10pF: I_out,max / CL = 100 uA / 10 pF = 10 V/us if current limited.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Class-AB push-pull output can provide peak current substantially higher than quiescent current, preventing severe slew limiting.

quiescent_power.description: Total DC power dissipation under static quiescent condition at VDD=1.8V

source.reference: Text on p. 794 regarding MON/MOP conducting 100 uA and bias circuit

equation.formula: P_diss = VDD * I_total = VDD * (I_first_stage + I_output_stage + I_bias)
equation.explanation: Total static current includes diff stage tail (~30 uA), cascode branches (~30 uA), output push-pull (~100 uA), and bias branches (~60 uA).
equation.assumptions: VDD = 1.8V, inputs biased at common-mode voltage 500 mV.

sky130_expected.calculation: Total supply current I_total ~ 220 uA. P_diss = 1.8 V * 220 uA = 396 uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Class-AB output stage sets quiescent current to ~100 uA; diff amp and bias network draw ~120 uA.

cmrr.description: Common-Mode Rejection Ratio of the op-amp at low frequencies

equation.explanation: CMRR is set by the ratio of differential gain to common-mode gain of the first stage cascode diff-amp.
equation.assumptions: Matched input pair and cascode loads.

sky130_expected.calculation: As stated on page 789: 'the CMRR is approximately 50 dB'. With cascoded tail source M6T/M6B, CMRR typically exceeds 60 dB in SKY130.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Cascode tail source increases common-mode output impedance, boosting CMRR.

psrr_positive.description: Power Supply Rejection Ratio from VDD to output at DC/low-frequency

equation.explanation: Ratio of open-loop differential gain to power supply gain from positive rail (VDD).
equation.assumptions: Indirect compensation node isolates Cc from VDD rail.

sky130_expected.calculation: Due to indirect feedback compensation connecting Cc to the source of M2T instead of node 1 directly, supply coupling is attenuated by cascode device isolation, providing PSRR+ > 60 dB at low frequencies.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Significantly better than Miller compensation where Cc shorts gate to drain of M7/MOP at high frequencies.

step3_testbench.description: Comprehensive ngspice testbench for the CMOS op-amp with output buffer (Fig. 24.29). Measures DC operating point, power dissipation, AC open-loop gain, unity-gain frequency, phase margin, CMRR, PSRR+, and transient large-signal step response with 1k resistor and 10pF load capacitor as in Fig. 24.31.
